html:
The great church of the popes in the Vatican, in Rome, built from 1506 to 1626 over the place where the apostle Peter is believed to be buried. It is the largest church in the world and the centre of the Catholic Church.

It replaced a basilica built by Constantine in the 300s, which was falling down after twelve centuries. Pope Julius II had the old church pulled down and began again to a plan by Bramante. The work took 120 years and passed through many hands, among them Raphael and Michelangelo, who designed the dome, 136 metres high. Bernini later added the bronze canopy over the altar and the curved colonnades of the square in front.

Paying for it changed Europe. The popes raised money by selling indulgences, and in 1517 Martin Luther attacked that sale in his ninety-five theses.
